changes: Uses much less of the Rytm's CPU when no sample is ping-ponging, which leaves more time for the screen and pads: in a large module set this was about 2 % of every audio block, even with LOP OFF everywhere.
No change to how LOP, PIPO or the zero snap play or look.
First library release, for Analog Rytm MKII OS 1.74: LOP gets a third value, PIPO, which plays the sample's loop forward, then backward.
Hold FUNC and turn STA or END to step to the next zero crossing, for loops without clicks.
Not yet tested on a unit: this exact build, several voices in PIPO, LOP locks and scenes, MIDI CC 30 and samples over 0.64 s.
Renamed Ping Pong Loop, and the module page now credits the author as Nathaniel Pavel (@npp1993). No change on the unit: LOP still reads PIPO.
